q: 1. The total thickness of flat slab, in no case, should be less than
explain: IS 456 specifies that the thickness of a flat slab shall be at least 125 mm to provide adequate stiffness and fire resistance.

q: 2. In four-way system of arranging the reinforcement, the reinforcement is provided in
explain: In a four-way reinforcement system for flat slabs, bars are placed in two sets of strips parallel to the center lines of columns and in two sets of diagonal strips.

q: 3. When a circular slab simply supported at the edge is loaded with uniformly distributed load, the stresses are developed in
explain: A loaded circular slab experiences bending in all directions, resulting in both radial and circumferential (hoop) moments and stresses.

q: 4. For a circular slab carrying a uniformly distributed load, the ratio of maximum negative radial moment and the maximum positive radial moment is equal to
explain: For a circular slab with fixed edges, the ratio of the negative moment at the support to the positive moment at the center is 2.0.

q: 5. A ribbed slab is provided where
explain: Ribbed slabs are efficient for long spans and provide voids that can be used for acoustic/thermal insulation or to hide services while maintaining a flat ceiling profile if covered.

q: 6. The thickness of the topping of a ribbed slab is kept from
explain: The topping (the thin slab on top of the ribs) typically varies between 50 mm to 80 mm depending on the spacing of the ribs.

q: 7. In a ribbed slab, the clear spacing between the ribs should not be more than
explain: Standard practice limits the clear spacing between ribs to 450 mm to ensure the topping slab can span between them effectively.

q: 8. For a ribbed slab, the overall depth, slab, should not be less than 75 mm...
explain: To ensure lateral stability of the ribs, the depth of the rib should not exceed four times its width.

q: 9. The diameter of a bar used in ribbed slab should not be more than
explain: Due to the narrow width of the ribs, the diameter of reinforcement is restricted; 22 mm is generally the maximum used to allow for proper concrete cover and flow.

q: 10. Enlarged head of a supporting column of a flat slab, is known as
explain: The flared or enlarged top of a column in a flat slab system is technically called the column capital.

q: 11. Thickened part of the flat slab over its supporting column is known as
explain: The drop panel is the portion of the slab that is thickened around the column to resist high shear and negative moments.

q: 12. The minimum amount of bottom reinforcement that should be continued over the entire length of the beam in R.C.C. continuous beam is
explain: At least one-third (33.33%) of the positive moment reinforcement must extend into the support to ensure structural integrity.

q: 13. The minimum amount of negative moment reinforcement in R.C.C. beams that should extend beyond the point of inflection is
explain: Standard practice requires at least 1/3 of the negative reinforcement to be extended beyond the point of inflection.

q: 14. The splicing of the reinforcement bars in R.C.C. beams can be done at a section where
options: bending moment is less than half the maximum B.M. on the beam
bending moment is more than half the maximum B.M. on the beam
explain: Splices should ideally be located away from sections of maximum stress; usually where the BM is less than 50% of the maximum BM.

q: 15. Lap splices in tension reinforcement are permitted for bars
explain: Lap splices are not recommended for bars larger than 36 mm; such bars should be welded or joined by mechanical couplers.

q: 16. The lap length of a direct, tension reinforcement bar in a R.C.C. beams should be more than
options: 30 times the diameter of the bar
twice the development length or 30 times the diameter of the bar
48 times the diameter of the bar
24 times the diameter of the bar or development length
explain: For direct tension, the lap length is taken as 2Ld or 30φ, whichever is greater, to ensure safety against sudden failure.

q: 17. The minimum horizontal distance between two main reinforcement bars should be
options: diameter of the larger bar or 5 mm more than the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate
5 mm more than the nominal size of the aggregate
5 mm more than the diameter of the bar
size of the aggregate of 5 mm more than the diameter of the bars
explain: To allow concrete to flow between bars, the gap must be at least the diameter of the bar or 5 mm more than the aggregate size.

q: 18. The minimum vertical space of the main reinforcement in R.C.C. beams is
options: diameter of the larger bar or 5 mm more than the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate
diameter of the larger bar or two-third the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate
explain: Vertical spacing is governed by several factors to ensure proper compaction; it should be at least 15mm, 2/3 aggregate size, or bar diameter.

q: 19. The maximum horizontal distance between parallel main reinforcement in beams is
explain: The code specifies maximum spacing limits to control crack widths; for Fe415, it is typically around 180mm, falling in the 125-235 range.

q: 20. The maximum horizontal distance between parallel main reinforcement bars in solid slabs is
options: 5 times the effective depth or 450 mm whichever is smaller
3 times the effective depth or 450 mm whichever is less
200 mm or 3 times the effective depth whichever is more
200 mm or 5 times the effective depth whichever is more
explain: For main reinforcement in slabs, IS 456 limits spacing to 3d or 300mm (the image says 450mm which was a value in older versions or for distribution bars).

q: 21. The minimum cover to the main bars in R.C.C. beam must be
options: 15 mm or diameter of the bar
25 mm or diameter of the bar
40 mm or diameter of the bar
25 mm or size of the coarse aggregate
explain: For beams, a nominal cover of 25 mm or the bar diameter (whichever is greater) is standard for moderate exposure.

q: 22. The minimum cover to the main reinforcement in R.C.C. solid slabs is
options: 15 mm or diameter of the bar
25 mm or diameter of the bar
40 mm or diameter of the bar
25 mm or size of the coarse aggregate
explain: Slabs have smaller cover requirements, typically 15 mm or the bar diameter.

q: 23. The final deflection due to all loads including the effects of temperature, creep and shrinkage should not normally exceed
options: span/250 or 20 mm whichever is less
span/350 or 20 mm whichever is less
explain: IS 456 limits the final deflection (including long-term effects) to Span/250 to prevent structural and aesthetic issues.

q: 24. The deflection including the effects of temperature, creep and shrinkage occurring after erection of partitions and the applications of finishes should not normally exceed
options: span/250 or 20 mm whichever is less
span/350 or 20 mm whichever is less
explain: For the safety of finishes and partitions, the deflection occurring after their application is strictly limited to Span/350 or 20 mm.

q: 25. For simply supported two way slabs of small spans with H.Y.S.D. bars of grade Fe415 the span to over all depth ratio is limited to
explain: For Fe415 steel in two-way slabs, the L/d ratio of 35 is multiplied by a factor (roughly 0.8), resulting in approximately 28.

q: 26. The minimum cover to the reinforcement of precast concrete piles is
explain: Piles are buried in soil (aggressive environment), requiring a higher cover of at least 40 mm.

q: 27. Which of the following is not a method for analyzing two way slabs with fixed edges?
explain: Hardy-Cross is a moment distribution method primarily used for continuous beams and rigid frames, not specifically for two-way slab analysis.

q: 28. The drop of a flat slab may have thickness........ more than the rest of the slab
explain: The drop panel is a thickened portion of the slab around the column designed to resist negative moments and punching shear; it typically increases slab thickness by 25% to 50%.

q: 29. The pitch of the main bars in a simply supported slab, should not exceed its effective depth by
explain: IS 456 specifies that the maximum spacing (pitch) for main tension reinforcement in slabs must not exceed 3 times the effective depth (3d) or 300 mm.

q: 30. Distribution reinforcement in a simply supported slab, is provided to distribute
explain: Secondary reinforcement (distribution bars) helps spread concentrated loads and controls cracking caused by temperature changes and concrete shrinkage.

q: 31. If the maximum bending moment of a simply supported slab is M kg. cm, the effective depth of the slab is
explain: From the formula M = Qbd², for unit width (b=100cm), d = √(M / 100Q).

q: 32. The floor slab of a building is supported on reinforced cement floor beams. The ratio of the end and intermediate spans is kept
explain: To achieve a more uniform bending moment across continuous spans, the end span is typically made slightly shorter (around 0.9 of intermediate span).

q: 33. The maximum ratio of span to depth of a cantilever slab, is
explain: For deflection control, the span-to-effective depth ratio for a cantilever is restricted to 7 (for basic values) or up to 12 depending on loading/reinforcement.

q: 34. The amount of reinforcement for main bars in a slab, is based upon
explain: Design reinforcement is always calculated to resist the maximum bending moment occurring at any critical section of the slab.

q: 35. In a slab, the pitch of the main reinforcement should not exceed its effective depth
explain: To ensure proper load distribution and crack control, the spacing of main bars is limited to 3 times the effective depth.

q: 36. The transverse reinforcement provided at right angles to the main reinforcement
explain: Transverse reinforcement (distribution steel) performs all these functions: load spreading, temperature resistance, and shrinkage control.

q: 37. If the diameter of the main reinforcement in a slab is 16 mm, the concrete cover to main bars is
explain: Nominal cover should generally not be less than the diameter of the bar (16 mm in this case) or the specified environmental cover (usually 15-20mm for slabs).

q: 38. If the ratio of long and short spans of a two way slab with corners held down is r, the actual reduction of B.M. is given by
explain: Based on Marcus's method for two-way slabs, the reduction factor involves the span ratio raised to the fourth power.

q: 39. According to I.S. 456, slabs which span in two directions with corners held down, are assumed to be divided in each direction into middle strips and edge strips such that the width of the middle strip, is
options: half of the width of the slab
two-third of the width of the slab
three-fourth of the width of the slab
four-fifth of the width of the slab
explain: IS 456 defines the middle strip as the central 3/4th (75%) of the span in each direction.

q: 40. If the sides of a slab simply supported on edges and spanning in two directions are equal, the maximum bending moment is multiplied by
explain: For a square slab (r=1), the load is shared equally in both directions, effectively halving the moment compared to a one-way slab.

q: 41. Design of a two way slab simply supported on edge and having no provision to prevent the corners from lifting is made by
explain: The Rankine-Grashoff theory is used for slabs where corners are free to lift, which assumes no torsional resistance at corners.

q: 42. The effective width of a column strip of flat slab, is
options: one-fourth the width of the panel
half the width of the panel
explain: In flat slab design, the column strip is defined as having a width equal to 50% (half) of the panel width.

q: 43. A circular slab subjected to external loading deflects to form a
explain: Due to uniform loading and radial symmetry, the elastic deflection curve of a circular plate/slab follows a paraboloid of revolution.

q: 44. For initial estimate for a beam design, the width is assumed
explain: A common rule of thumb for initial sizing of beam width is approximately 1/30th of the span.

q: 45. The maximum permissible size of aggregate to be used in casing the ribs of a slab, is
explain: In ribbed slabs with thin sections, 10 mm aggregate is used to ensure the concrete can flow around the closely spaced reinforcement.

q: 46. A very comfortable type of stairs is
explain: Open newel stairs provide a central well for ventilation and light, making them more spacious and comfortable for users.

q: 47. The minimum head room over a stair must be
explain: Note: In the options provided '200 mm' is marked as 'd' in the key, though technically 200 cm (2m) is the standard clearance for safety.

q: 48. For stairs spanning horizontally, the minimum waist provided is
explain: The waist slab thickness for horizontally spanning stairs is typically kept at a minimum of 8 cm to ensure structural rigidity.

q: 49. For stairs spanning l meters longitudinally between supports at the bottom and of a flight carrying a load w per unit horizontal area, the maximum bending moment per metre width, is
explain: Like a simply supported beam, a longitudinally spanning stair flight experiences a maximum moment of wl²/8.

q: 50. If longitudinally spanning stairs are casted along with their landings, the maximum bending moment per metre width, is taken as
explain: Casting with landings creates partial continuity, which reduces the effective maximum bending moment to approximately wl²/10.
